title: Rise in Use of "Buy Now, Pay Later" Schemes among Young Consumers and Its Impact on Risk of Over-spending and Credit Assessments
what_it_is: Rise in Use of "Buy Now, Pay Later" Schemes among Young Consumers and Its Impact on Risk of Over-spending and Credit Assessments

sections.label: BNPL Code and credit checks
sections.summary: MAS does not regulate BNPL firms, but accredited firms follow a Code of Conduct with age, credit and assessment rules.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: While the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) does not currently regulate BNPL firms, those operating in Singapore have committed to the BNPL Code of Conduct that was developed under MAS' guidance to mitigate the risk of debt accumulation and to protect the user interests.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Under the BNPL Code, accredited firms can only offer BNPL services to customers aged 18 years and above, and are not allowed to extend more than $2,000 in credit to a customer unless they conduct an additional credit assessment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The credit assessment includes conducting income checks and credit checks against the BNPL credit bureau, which includes information on BNPL users' outstanding balances, missed payments and delinquencies amongst accredited firms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The Total Debt Servicing Ratio (TDSR) includes monthly debt obligations from all credit facilities granted by financial institutions regulated by MAS.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: MAS does not require financial institutions to include outstanding BNPL amounts when computing the TDSR requirements, recognising that BNPL outstanding amounts tend to be relatively small with safeguards to prevent snowballing.

sections.label: MAS monitoring BNPL sector
sections.summary: MAS continues to monitor BNPL sector developments and will review its regulatory framework as appropriate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: MAS continues to monitor developments in the BNPL sector and will review its regulatory framework as appropriate.

sections.label: BNPL credit bureau and accreditation
sections.summary: A BNPL credit bureau shares outstanding amounts and delinquency status, and all four BNPL firms are accredited to the Code.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: I have mentioned that in previous Parliamentary replies, but I also wanted to highlight that there is also a BNPL credit bureau which shares information on customers' outstanding amounts and delinquency status.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: I also wanted to let the Member know that all four BNPL firms are now accredited to the BNPL Code and they must ensure customers that fail to pay on time are not able to use their BNPL services to make additional purchases.

sections.label: Youths, borrowing and responsibility
sections.summary: Youths with BNPL purchases mentioned cost of living, expenditure choices and living beyond their means, so regulator, industry and borrowers must play their part.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: One big takeaway was this - many of the youths there who had BNPL purchases spoke of cost of living, but they also mentioned their choices of living in terms of expenditure and also living beyond their means.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: So, in short: regulator must play their part; industry must play their part; but so too borrowers must play their part.
